description: `cli-health validate <scenario>` returns schema errors, unresolved `binding.service`/`binding.method` references, orphan proto methods, and stale omission entries; exits nonzero on any error-level finding.

requirements.description: The `cli-health validate <scenario>` command must validate the scenario's `cli/manifest.json` against the canonical `.vrooli/schemas/cli-manifest.schema.json`. Every schema violation must be reported as an error-level finding with a unique finding code, a human-readable message, and the JSON path of the offending field. The command must exit with a nonzero exit code when one or more error-level findings are present.
requirements.title: JSON Schema Validation for CLI Manifest

validation.notes: Given a manifest missing a required top-level field, validate returns a finding with code SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD and the correct JSON path
Given a manifest with a field of the wrong type, validate returns a finding with code SCHEMA_TYPE_MISMATCH
Given a fully valid manifest, validate returns zero schema findings
Given any error-level finding, the process exits with exit code 1
Given only warning-level findings, the process exits with exit code 0
Run `cli-health validate` against all 6 currently-adopting scenario manifests and assert zero schema findings
Inject a known schema violation into one adopting scenario manifest copy and assert nonzero exit code and correct finding code
Schema validation catches malformed manifests before they reach runtime, preventing misconfigured CLI discovery

requirements.description: The `cli-health validate <scenario>` command must resolve every `binding.service` and `binding.method` reference in the manifest against the compiled proto descriptor set for that scenario. Any reference that cannot be resolved to a known service or method in the descriptor set must be reported as an error-level finding with finding code UNRESOLVED_BINDING, including the unresolved service FQN and method name. The command must exit nonzero when any such finding is present.
requirements.title: Binding Reference Resolution Against Proto Descriptors

validation.notes: Given a manifest binding referencing a service not present in the descriptor set, validate returns UNRESOLVED_BINDING with the correct service FQN
Given a manifest binding referencing a valid service but a nonexistent method, validate returns UNRESOLVED_BINDING with the method name
Given all bindings resolving correctly against the descriptor set, validate returns zero binding findings
Unit tests use synthetic proto descriptor sets generated from minimal .proto files
Parameterized test: for each of the 6 adopting scenarios, run validate and assert all binding references resolve against that scenario's real descriptor set
Mutate one binding in a test manifest copy to reference a nonexistent method and assert UNRESOLVED_BINDING finding and nonzero exit
Unresolved bindings would cause silent runtime failures in CLI routing; deterministic validation prevents this

requirements.description: The `cli-health validate <scenario>` command must detect (a) orphan proto methods: RPC methods present in the descriptor set that are neither bound in the manifest nor listed in the `omitted[]` array, reported as error-level finding ORPHAN_METHOD; and (b) stale omission entries: entries in `omitted[]` that no longer correspond to any method in the descriptor set, reported as error-level finding STALE_OMISSION. Both finding types must trigger a nonzero exit code. No additions to `.vrooli/schemas/cli-manifest.schema.json` are permitted; the existing `omitted[]` field is used as-is.
requirements.title: Orphan Proto Method and Stale Omission Detection

validation.notes: Given a descriptor set containing method Foo not in manifest bindings and not in omitted[], validate returns ORPHAN_METHOD for Foo
Given method Foo in omitted[] but absent from descriptor set, validate returns STALE_OMISSION for Foo
Given all descriptor methods either bound or in omitted[], and all omitted[] entries present in descriptor, validate returns zero orphan/stale findings
Per-finding-code unit tests use synthetic manifests and descriptor sets
Parameterized validation across all 6 adopting scenarios asserts zero orphan method and stale omission findings
Add a synthetic method to a test descriptor and assert ORPHAN_METHOD is produced
Orphan methods represent undocumented CLI surface area; stale omissions indicate manifest drift from the proto source of truth

title: Deterministic manifest validation
